info.name: Event Ticketing: API and server (Builds 1 to 3)
info.description:
POST and GET requests for the Event Ticketing API, with automatic checks on every response.

1. Start the server in DEMO mode:  npm run start:demo   (http://localhost:3000)
2. Import this file and postman/local.postman_environment.json, choose the "Event Ticketing: local" environment.
3. Run the collection in ORDER (Collection Runner). Folders 2 to 5 pass ids from one request to the next with collection variables, so run them top to bottom. Folder 5 needs demo mode (a normal start answers 404 there).

Every response is also checked for an X-Request-Id header and, for errors, the exact shape { error: { code, message } } with no stack trace.

exec: // Runs after EVERY request in this collection.
pm.test('has a request id (quote it when reporting a problem)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.has('X-Request-Id')).to.be.true);
pm.test('error: no stack trace reaches the client', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/\n\s+at |node:internal|\.js:\d+|node_modules/));

request.description: The required check: the server is up and answers.
HEAD is GET without the body.

exec: pm.test('the query string changes nothing', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ status: 'ok' }); });
pm.test('a trailing slash is ignored', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('ok'); });

item.name: 2. Events: create, add tiers, publish, read (POST + GET)

exec: // A fresh label for this run, and an event date 30 days from now (17:00 Lagos time).
pm.test('a new id, and the event is a DRAFT', () => { pm.expect(event.id).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(event.status).to.eql('draft'); });
pm.test('Location header points at the new event', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.eql('/api/events/' + event.id));
pm.test('no tiers yet, and no internal fields', () => { pm.expect(event.tiers).to.eql([]); pm.expect(event).to.not.have.property('tierIds'); });

request.description: Creates a PRIVATE draft. The pre-request script makes a fresh runTag and a date 30 days away, so you can run this again and again.

exec: pm.test('it is the event we created, still a draft', () => { pm.expect(event.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('eventId')); pm.expect(event.status).to.eql('draft'); });

request.description: A draft can be read by its id. It is only hidden from the public LIST.

item.name: 2.3 GET /api/events: the draft is NOT on the public list

exec: pm.test('count is 0: drafts are private', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ count: 0, events: [] }));

request.description: Searches for this run's tag. A draft never shows.

exec: pm.test('saved with 0 sold and 3 seats left', () => { pm.expect(tier.sold).to.eql(0); pm.expect(tier.seatsLeft).to.eql(3); pm.expect(tier.capacity).to.eql(3); });
pm.test('the price is a whole number of kobo', () => pm.expect(tier.priceCents).to.eql(500000));

request.description: Money is always whole kobo: 500000 = N5,000.00. Capacity 3 makes it easy to sell out later.
Needs at least one tier (try publishing an event with no tiers: 409 INVALID_STATE).

item.name: 2.7 GET /api/events: now it IS on the public list

exec: pm.test('the summary shows the CHEAPEST tier and the seats left in ALL tiers', () => { pm.expect(found.minPriceCents).to.eql(500000); pm.expect(found.seatsLeft).to.eql(4); pm.expect(found.tierCount).to.eql(2); });

item.name: 2.8 GET /api/events/:id: the event with both tiers

exec: pm.test('two tiers, in the order they were added', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().event.tiers.map((t) => t.name)).to.eql(['General', 'VIP']));

item.name: 3.1 Setup: create a second event (later and dearer)

request.description: Event B starts 40 days away, costs more, and has more seats. That makes the three sort orders DIFFERENT below.

item.name: 3.2 Setup: add a tier to event B
3.4 GET ?q=: search by text (capital letters do not matter)

exec: pm.test('searched in lower case, and still found both events', () => { pm.expect(pm.collectionVariables.get('runTagLower')).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('runTag')); pm.expect(pm.response.json().count).to.eql(2); });

request.description: The tag is searched in LOWER case ("pm..."), but the titles contain it in capitals ("PM..."). Matches the title or the venue.

exec: pm.test('only Postman Jazz', () => { const titles = pm.response.json().events.map((e) => e.title); pm.expect(titles).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(titles[0]).to.include('Jazz'); });

request.description: Searches for the word Jazz followed by this run's tag, so earlier runs' events can never be counted.

exec: pm.test('both events are in Postmanville', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().events.every((e) => e.city === 'Postmanville')).to.be.true);

request.description: City is matched whole and ignoring capitals. The tag keeps this run's events apart from earlier runs'.

exec: pm.test('an empty list is a normal 200', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.eql({ count: 0, events: [] }));
pm.test('only the N5,000 event (event B costs N9,000)', () => { const e = pm.response.json().events; pm.expect(e).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(e[0].minPriceCents).to.eql(500000); });

request.description: Compares with the CHEAPEST tier of each event. 500000 itself is allowed.

item.name: 3.10 GET ?from=&to=: a date range (the "to" day is included)

exec: pm.test('event A (30 days away, 17:00) is inside; event B (40 days) is not', () => { const e = pm.response.json().events; pm.expect(e).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(e[0].id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('eventId')); });

request.description: A date-only "to" means the END of that day, so an event at 5 PM that day is included.

exec: pm.test('A (30 days) before B (40 days)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().events.map((e) => e.id)).to.eql([pm.collectionVariables.get('eventId'), pm.collectionVariables.get('eventB')]));
pm.test('B (10 seats) before A (4 seats)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().events.map((e) => e.seatsLeft)).to.eql([10, 4]));

request.description: Compare with the two requests above: three sorts, three different orders.

exec: pm.test('the message says what is wrong', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.include('maxPriceCents'));

request.description: There is no 30 February.

item.name: 3.17 GET ?citty=Lagos: a typo in an option -> 400

request.description: An option that does not exist is refused, so a typo can't silently show everything.

exec: pm.test('a PENDING booking for 2 seats', () => { pm.expect(booking.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(booking.quantity).to.eql(2); });
pm.test('Location header points at the booking', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.eql('/api/bookings/' + booking.reference));

request.description: The tier has 3 seats, so 1 will be left.
Codes are read aloud over the phone, so they forgive capitals, spaces and the hyphen.

exec: pm.test('the message says how many are left', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.include('Only 1 left'));

request.description: Nothing changes when a booking is refused.
The quantity must be a JSON NUMBER, not the text "2".
The limit is 10 per booking.

item.name: 4.9 POST /api/bookings: a tier that does not exist -> 404
4.10 POST /api/bookings: tries to set its own status and price

exec: pm.test('the extra fields were IGNORED: still pending, price worked out by the server', () => { pm.expect(booking.status).to.eql('pending'); pm.expect(booking.totalCents).to.eql(500000); });

request.description: A client may not choose its own status or price. (This takes the last seat, so cancel it in 4.11.)

exec: pm.test('cancelled, with the history recorded', () => { pm.expect(body.booking.status).to.eql('cancelled'); pm.expect(body.booking.history.map((h) => h.status)).to.eql(['pending', 'cancelled']); });
pm.test('all 3 seats are free again', () => pm.expect(body.seatsLeft).to.eql(3));

request.description: The seats are NOT given back twice.

item.name: 4.15 POST /api/events/:id/unpublish: take event B off the list
4.16 POST /api/bookings: a DRAFT cannot be booked -> 409
4.17 POST /api/events/:id/publish: event B is public again
5. Booking life cycle (DEMO MODE: npm run start:demo)

request.description: Needs demo mode: npm run start:demo. In a normal start this URL is a 404.

exec: pm.test('the history is the whole story', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().booking.history.map((h) => h.status)).to.eql(['pending', 'paid', 'checked_in']));
pm.test('it explains why: checked_in is final', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.include('final'));

request.description: checked_in is a FINAL state: nothing can leave it.

exec: pm.test('the exact sentence from the brief', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.include('cancelled booking cannot become paid'));

request.description: The headline of Build 3: paying a cancelled booking is refused by the state machine.

item.name: 5.10 a state that does not exist: REFUSED
5.14 GET /api/events/:id: the refund gave the seat back

exec: pm.test('2 seats left: one is held by the checked-in booking, the cancelled and refunded ones are free', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().event.tiers.find((t) => t.name === 'General').seatsLeft).to.eql(2));

request.description: Anything under /api that has no route.

exec: pm.test('the Allow header lists what works', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Allow')).to.eql('GET, HEAD'));

request.description: POST to a path that only answers GET.

exec: pm.test('the message does not repeat the body', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('"title"'));

request.description: The body is cut off in the middle, so it is not valid JSON.

item.name: Valid JSON to an unknown API path -> 404

exec: pm.test('the JSON was fine, but there is no such route: 404', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

request.description: Compare with the Bad JSON request above: this body is valid, and there is no such route, so it is a plain 404. (It uses /api/unknown-thing: /api/events is a real route now.)
The header says text/plain, so the server will not read it as JSON.
Even a missing FILE answers with the standard error JSON.
There is no 30 February.

item.name: POST /api/events with the JSON value null -> 400 (not a crash)

exec: pm.test('a bad body is the CLIENT\'s mistake (400), never a server bug (500)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.not.eql(500));

request.description: "null" is valid JSON. It used to crash the booking and tier code with a 500 before this was tested.

exec: pm.test('it is the Event Ticketing page', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.include('Event Ticketing'));
pm.test('the browser may only load things from this server', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Security-Policy')).to.include("default-src 'self'"));
pm.test('the browser must not guess the type', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Content-Type-Options')).to.eql('nosniff'));

pm.test('the project\'s package.json did not leak', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('event-ticketing'));
